This is consistent with a standard Ambetter ACA marketplace appeals process (180-day internal appeal deadline, matching the letter). I have enough to compile the answer, being explicit about where the UKA-specific criteria text was corroborated.

## Findings

**1–2. Governing policy identified**

The document Louisiana Healthcare Connections uses to make medical-necessity determinations for knee arthroplasty (including CPT 27446, unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty) is a clinical guideline maintained by **Evolent** (the vendor Louisiana Healthcare Connections delegates musculoskeletal-surgery prior authorization/utilization management to, formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA). I located and read a copy of this guideline posted publicly by the Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) as part of its Medicaid managed-care policy repository, expressly labeled for Louisiana Healthcare Connections (LHCC):

- **Title:** Evolent Clinical Guideline 1763 for Knee Arthroplasty
- **Guideline/Policy number:** Evolent_CG_1763
- **URL:** https://ldh.la.gov/assets/medicaid/MCPP/7_15_25/1882_LHCC_Knee_Arthroplasty.pdf
- **Original date:** November 2015
- **Last revised date:** shown in the document with tracked-change text as "December 2023 → November 2024" (i.e., most recently revised November 2024)
- **Implementation date:** shown as "January 2024 → January 2025" (i.e., implemented January 2025)
- Applicable lines of business checked in the document: CHIP, **Commercial**, **Exchange/Marketplace**, and Medicaid — consistent with the member's ACA plan.

Note on confidence: my automated PDF extraction of this exact LDH-hosted file truncated after the Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) section (the table of contents confirms a dedicated "Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty (UKA)/Partial Knee Replacement (PKA)" section beginning on page 6, immediately followed by "Contraindications for Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA," which is the section governing CPT 27446). I was able to independently retrieve the *verbatim* text of that UKA/PKA section from another payer's public medical-policy page that also implements the identical Evolent Clinical Guideline 1763 language (Healthy Blue's "Knee Arthroplasty – CAM.775HB" policy). The general-requirements/TKA text matches word-for-word between the two sources, which gives me good (not perfect) confidence that the UKA/PKA criteria quoted below match what appears in the LHCC copy of Guideline 1763 — but I could not directly confirm that exact page of the LHCC file itself.

**3. Medical-necessity criteria for CPT 27446 (Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA)**

> "Medial or lateral UKA/PKA may be medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:
> - At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment
> - Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Weight reduction for individual with elevated BMI; Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Physician-supervised exercise program (including home exercise program); Application of heat or ice; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics; Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation
> - Total arc of motion (goniometer) > 90 degrees
> - Normal ACL or stable reconstructed ACL per physical exam test
> - Contracture ≤ 10 degrees upon physical exam (goniometer)
> - Angular deformity ≤ 10 degrees, passively correctable to neutral upon physical exam (goniometer)
> - Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration
> - NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint
> - No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery
> - No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery"

> "Contraindications for Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA: Any corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery; Any prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery; Local or systemic active infection; Inflammatory arthritis; Angular deformity or contracture greater than indicated range; Significant arthritic involvement of opposite compartment; ACL instability; Poor bone quality or significant osteoporosis or osteopenia; Meniscectomy of the opposite compartment, involving > 25% of meniscus; Stiffness greater than indicated range of motion."

Also applicable are the guideline's **general requirements** for elective knee arthroplasty (confirmed directly in the LHCC-hosted PDF text I retrieved), including documented knee pain with loss of function, medical stability/optimization for surgery, absence of active infection, absence of untreated drug dependency, and good oral hygiene, plus documentation of symptom history, function loss, and non-operative treatment trial (at least two of the listed conservative measures).

**4. Appeal deadline**

As stated in the denial notice: the internal appeal must be **received within 180 days of the August 15, 2026 notice date, i.e., by February 11, 2027**. This is consistent with the standard ACA/Marketplace internal-appeal deadline used by Ambetter/Louisiana Healthcare Connections plans.

**5. Where/how to submit the appeal**

Per the plan's published Appeals/Reconsiderations and Grievances Guide (Ambetter from Louisiana Healthcare Connections):

- **Mail:** Ambetter Appeals and Grievances Department, P.O. Box 10341, Van Nuys, CA 91410
- **Email:** ambetter_centralized_Grievances_Appeals@CENTENE.com
- **Fax:** 1-833-886-7956
- Members may also file by phone through Member/Customer Service, and providers may file on the member's behalf with a signed Appointment of Representative (AOR) form if the request is submitted by someone other than a treating participating physician.
- Include: a cover letter identifying the specific CPT code/service being appealed (27446), the reference number (POC-CD20076A7A-66146), a summary of the appeal, and all supporting medical records (clinic notes, physical exam findings including goniometer measurements of motion/contracture/deformity, weight-bearing X-ray reports with Kellgren-Lawrence grading, ACL exam findings, and documentation of at least 12 weeks of the required conservative treatments) addressing each Evolent CG 1763 UKA/PKA criterion above.
- If the internal appeal is denied, the notice should also describe the right to request external review by an Independent Review Organization (IRO), typically within 180 days of the final internal denial — the patient should confirm this exact language and deadline in the internal-appeal decision letter when it arrives.

## Findings

**1–2. Governing policy identified**

The document Louisiana Healthcare Connections uses to make medical-necessity determinations for knee arthroplasty (including CPT 27446, unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty) is a clinical guideline maintained by **Evolent** (the vendor Louisiana Healthcare Connections delegates musculoskeletal-surgery prior authorization/utilization management to, formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA). I located and read a copy of this guideline posted publicly by the Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) as part of its Medicaid managed-care policy repository, expressly labeled for Louisiana Healthcare Connections (LHCC):

- **Title:** Evolent Clinical Guideline 1763 for Knee Arthroplasty
- **Guideline/Policy number:** Evolent_CG_1763
- **URL:** https://ldh.la.gov/assets/medicaid/MCPP/7_15_25/1882_LHCC_Knee_Arthroplasty.pdf
- **Original date:** November 2015
- **Last revised date:** shown in the document with tracked-change text as "December 2023 → November 2024" (i.e., most recently revised November 2024)
- **Implementation date:** shown as "January 2024 → January 2025" (i.e., implemented January 2025)
- Applicable lines of business checked in the document: CHIP, **Commercial**, **Exchange/Marketplace**, and Medicaid — consistent with the member's ACA plan.

Note on confidence: my automated PDF extraction of this exact LDH-hosted file truncated after the Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) section (the table of contents confirms a dedicated "Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty (UKA)/Partial Knee Replacement (PKA)" section beginning on page 6, immediately followed by "Contraindications for Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA," which is the section governing CPT 27446). I was able to independently retrieve the *verbatim* text of that UKA/PKA section from another payer's public medical-policy page that also implements the identical Evolent Clinical Guideline 1763 language (Healthy Blue's "Knee Arthroplasty – CAM.775HB" policy). The general-requirements/TKA text matches word-for-word between the two sources, which gives me good (not perfect) confidence that the UKA/PKA criteria quoted below match what appears in the LHCC copy of Guideline 1763 — but I could not directly confirm that exact page of the LHCC file itself.

**3. Medical-necessity criteria for CPT 27446 (Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA)**

> "Medial or lateral UKA/PKA may be medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:
> - At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment
> - Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Weight reduction for individual with elevated BMI; Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Physician-supervised exercise program (including home exercise program); Application of heat or ice; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics; Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation
> - Total arc of motion (goniometer) > 90 degrees
> - Normal ACL or stable reconstructed ACL per physical exam test
> - Contracture ≤ 10 degrees upon physical exam (goniometer)
> - Angular deformity ≤ 10 degrees, passively correctable to neutral upon physical exam (goniometer)
> - Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration
> - NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint
> - No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery
> - No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery"

> "Contraindications for Medial or Lateral UKA/PKA: Any corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery; Any prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery; Local or systemic active infection; Inflammatory arthritis; Angular deformity or contracture greater than indicated range; Significant arthritic involvement of opposite compartment; ACL instability; Poor bone quality or significant osteoporosis or osteopenia; Meniscectomy of the opposite compartment, involving > 25% of meniscus; Stiffness greater than indicated range of motion."

Also applicable are the guideline's **general requirements** for elective knee arthroplasty (confirmed directly in the LHCC-hosted PDF text I retrieved), including documented knee pain with loss of function, medical stability/optimization for surgery, absence of active infection, absence of untreated drug dependency, and good oral hygiene, plus documentation of symptom history, function loss, and non-operative treatment trial (at least two of the listed conservative measures).

**4. Appeal deadline**

As stated in the denial notice: the internal appeal must be **received within 180 days of the August 15, 2026 notice date, i.e., by February 11, 2027**. This is consistent with the standard ACA/Marketplace internal-appeal deadline used by Ambetter/Louisiana Healthcare Connections plans.

**5. Where/how to submit the appeal**

Per the plan's published Appeals/Reconsiderations and Grievances Guide (Ambetter from Louisiana Healthcare Connections):

- **Mail:** Ambetter Appeals and Grievances Department, P.O. Box 10341, Van Nuys, CA 91410
- **Email:** ambetter_centralized_Grievances_Appeals@CENTENE.com
- **Fax:** 1-833-886-7956
- Members may also file by phone through Member/Customer Service, and providers may file on the member's behalf with a signed Appointment of Representative (AOR) form if the request is submitted by someone other than a treating participating physician.
- Include: a cover letter identifying the specific CPT code/service being appealed (27446), the reference number (POC-CD20076A7A-66146), a summary of the appeal, and all supporting medical records (clinic notes, physical exam findings including goniometer measurements of motion/contracture/deformity, weight-bearing X-ray reports with Kellgren-Lawrence grading, ACL exam findings, and documentation of at least 12 weeks of the required conservative treatments) addressing each Evolent CG 1763 UKA/PKA criterion above.
- If the internal appeal is denied, the notice should also describe the right to request external review by an Independent Review Organization (IRO), typically within 180 days of the final internal denial — the patient should confirm this exact language and deadline in the internal-appeal decision letter when it arrives.
